entities.name: Security header type
entities.description: A 4-bit information element in bits 5-8 of the first octet of every EMM message containing control information related to NAS message security protection.

entities.name: Plain NAS message
entities.description: An EMM message that is not security protected, indicated by security header type 0000.

entities.name: SECURITY MODE COMMAND
entities.description: A NAS message that can only use security header type 0011 (integrity protected with new EPS security context).

entities.name: SECURITY MODE COMPLETE
entities.description: A NAS message that can only use security header type 0100 (integrity protected and ciphered with new EPS security context).

entities.name: SERVICE REQUEST
entities.description: A NAS message that uses security header type 1100, with bits 5-6 reserved for future extensions.

entities.name: CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST
entities.description: A NAS message that can only use security header type 0101 (integrity protected and partially ciphered).

entities.name: Security header type 0000
entities.description: Indicates a plain NAS message that is not security protected.

entities.name: Security header type 1100-1111
entities.description: Values 1100-1111 are interpreted as 1100 in this protocol version, with bits 5-6 reserved for SERVICE REQUEST extensions.

relations.description: Security header type 0000 indicates a plain NAS message without security protection.
Security header type 0011 is exclusively used for SECURITY MODE COMMAND messages.
Security header type 0100 is exclusively used for SECURITY MODE COMPLETE messages.
Security header type 1100 is used for SERVICE REQUEST messages with bits 5-6 reserved for future extensions.
Security header type 0101 is exclusively used for CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST messages.
When security header type is 0000, the message is treated as a plain NAS message without security protection.
Security header types 1100-1111 are interpreted as 1100 for SERVICE REQUEST messages in this protocol version.
